verse.text: The righteous person may have many troubles, but the Lord delivers him from them all;

reflection.scripture: The righteous person may have many troubles, but the Lord delivers him from them all;
reflection.observation: The psalmist doesn't promise a trouble-free life for the righteous — in fact, he says the opposite. Many troubles will come. But the promise isn't absence of hardship; it's presence of deliverance. God doesn't remove us from every storm, but He walks through them with us, carrying us when we can't stand. This is the kind of hope that sustains a daily faith practice — not naive optimism, but grounded assurance.
reflection.application: When troubles come today — and they will — resist the urge to ask 'Why me?' and instead ask 'What now?' Look for one small way God might be delivering you in this moment: a friend's text, a quiet moment of peace, strength you didn't think you had. Write it down in your SOAP journal. The act of noticing God's deliverance trains your heart to see it more clearly.
reflection.prayer: Lord, I don't pray for a life without trouble — I pray for eyes that see Your deliverance in the middle of it. When I'm overwhelmed, remind me that You are nearer than my next breath. Help me to be honest about my struggles and faithful in my trust. Deliver me, Lord — not just from my circumstances, but into deeper dependence on You. Amen.
